messages:
maya: quick sync — we need a concrete telemetry contract for the token/unit-econ dashboard. primary asks: cost per 1k tokens, cache/batch savings breakdown, and per-route unit costs. thoughts?
jason: @maya yep. two quick Qs: do we want runtime to emit pre- or post-cost counts? i prefer runtime emits raw counters + cache events and let analytics compute billed tokens. that keeps runtime simple.
liam: +1. runtime should emit these fields: `tokens_total`, `tokens_cached_hit`, `tokens_cached_miss`, `kv_cache_saved_tokens`, `batch_size`, `model_variant`, `quantized`, `seq_len`. downstream does `billable = tokens_total - tokens_cached_hit - kv_cache_saved_tokens - batch_saved`.
maya: Sophie — on console UX, how should we present the savings breakdown so it's intuitive for customers?
sophie: propose 3 widgets: 1) Cost per 1k tokens line chart (toggle committed vs spot pricing), 2) Savings waterfall (raw tokens -> cache hits -> batch savings -> billed tokens -> cost), 3) per-route heatmap for p50/p95 latency + unit cost. need `route`, `tenant_id_hash`, `region`, `routing_policy` fields in telemetry for filters.
jason: draft telemetry json (runtime -> ingest):
```
{
  "timestamp": "...",
  "tenant_id_hash": "...",
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "model": "redwood-13b-v2",
  "model_variant": "int8",
  "tokens_total": 1024,
  "tokens_cached_hit": 256,
  "kv_cache_saved_tokens": 128,
  "batch_size": 4,
  "avg_latency_ms": 120,
  "p95_latency_ms": 340,
  "routing_policy": "latency",
  "fallback": "none",
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "gpu_ms": 45
}
```
jason: also recommend runtime emit `gpu_ms` + `gpu_type` so infra can map to cost factors. we can keep `hardware_cost_usd` computed in analytics to centralize pricing.
liam: runtime can add `gpu_ms` and `gpu_type`. will put `emit_unit_econ_v2` behind a feature flag. also will emit sample_count for batched requests so we can attribute batch savings precisely.
maya: note on privacy/compliance — tenant_id must be hashed with org salt. no PII. also need to avoid storing raw prompt text in the telemetry layer.
sophie: UX: add an "explain savings" drilldown that shows an example request trace and highlights tokens avoided by cache vs batch. customers can sample traces for 30 days.
deploy-bot: ingest-pipeline v2 deployed to staging; mapping now accepts `kv_cache_saved_tokens` and `gpu_ms` (staging).
jason: next steps: runtime team (liam) add fields by EOD Wed behind flag; eng-platform (me/maya) add parser/ETL mapping; analytics to implement cost calc and a prototype dashboard. who will own rollout plan?
maya: i'll coordinate rollout. plan: canary per-tenant sampling 1% -> 10% -> 100% with automated sanity checks. rollback triggers: >10% delta in billed tokens or >15% jump in average.unit cost vs baseline.
liam: i'll land a unit test and link the feature-flag PR. also will include an integration test that simulates cache hits + batch composition.
sophie: i'll mock the console widgets and post a Figma link in #design later today.
jason: small API debate: should `kv_cache_saved_tokens` be sub-field of `cache` object or top-level int? i vote top-level ints for easier ingestion (less nested mapping).
maya: i'm fine with top-level for now, we can iterate. just document the schema in the onboarding ticket.
liam: will add schema to runtime repo and a short README snippet on how `billable` should be computed.
maya: thanks all — i'll open a tracking ticket and tag everyone. will include sample queries and the waterfall spec. :thumbsup:
sophie: thanks! excited to see the savings visualized.
deploy-bot: canary schedule created: 1900503300 -> 1900503360 -> 1900503420
